change: an execution's own brief, and everything that brief's input table pins, are pinned by it while it runs

defect.found: 2026-09-15, during the c01 primaries pilot; re-measured with eight executions in flight
defect.class: a safety control that fails OPEN, weaker than the hand-written playbook line it exists to enforce
defect.observed: with eight primaries in flight the guard returned CLEAR on Ezek/PRIMARY_BRIEF_LF.md, Ezek/PRIMARY_BRIEF_OL.md, Ezek/repair/rows_v7_cwo24.jsonl and Ezek/review_clusters.json - the brief each agent is reading and the corpus and cluster plan each agent binds by digest
defect.root_cause: pins_for only parsed files that NAME the execution. PRIMARY_BRIEF_LF.md is shared by all 22 literary-form primaries, names none of them, carries no template id and does not list itself, so neither the brief nor ANY line of its input table was ever reachable for a primary. The earlier rules (execution id, template id, attempt-id fallback) all key on the brief naming the agent; nothing keyed on the agent naming the brief.
defect.blast_radius_if_unfixed: any orchestrator write to the v7 corpus, the cluster plan, the device inventory or either brief during a 36-execution wave would have passed the guard and silently broken 8-16 running reviewers' digest bindings at once - the OW-11-i incident that created this tool, at wave scale
defect.l0035_correction: L-0035 recorded the cure as 'the launch record already names each execution's brief; the guard should treat that path as pinned'. The first clause was FALSE: no transcript-map entry has ever carried a brief field. The launch MESSAGE named the brief; the durable record did not. Fixing the guard alone would have changed nothing, which is why this change has two halves and why the inertness regression below passed.

what_changed: own_briefs(): reads a `brief`/`brief_path`/`orders`/`orders_path` field off every transcript-map entry and normalises it to an SP-relative path (accepts `SP\Book\x.md`, `Book/x.md`, or absolute inside SP)

pins_for(): takes the execution's own-brief map; the brief counts as pinned whether or not it lists itself, and its file is added to the set whose input table is parsed, so every path that table pins counts too
check(): computes the launch records once and passes each execution its own slice
the transcript map is now read with utf-8-sig in both readers that open it, instead of utf-8 in one
what_did_not_change: every earlier rule and every earlier verdict: the ten original selftest vectors pass unchanged, and on ten real targets the candidate's output was byte-identical to the preimage's while no launch record carried a brief field

selftest_vectors_added: the shared brief an in-flight execution is recorded as reading -> PINNED
a file in that shared brief's input table -> PINNED
a brief only a LANDED execution was reading -> CLEAR
a file in a landed execution's brief table -> CLEAR
every reader of one shared brief is named, not just the first
own-brief pin released when both readers land (brief and table file)

real_tree_regression.what: preimage vs candidate, same 10 real targets, same book, while no transcript-map entry carried a brief field
real_tree_regression.reading: the fix is INERT until a launch record names a brief, which is also the proof that L-0035's premise was wrong: if the map had already named each execution's brief, these verdicts would have differed here

limits: the guard protects only what a launch record names. An execution whose map entry has no brief field is still invisible to this rule; post_launch_primary.py now writes the field, and any other launcher must too.
a pin written as an absolute path OUTSIDE SP is still not detected (pre-existing limitation, unchanged)

runtime is O(targets x in-flight) full re-reads of the book's briefs; at eight in flight and ten targets one run takes minutes. Recorded as a separate defect: a control slow enough to tempt an orchestrator into skipping it is a weak control.
